category_title: Young students with EBD, ADHD, and ODD exhibiting noncompliance and disrobing behaviors
minimal_context: Axel is sitting in his individual work area being asked to complete a reading assignment by his teacher.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Axel, it is time to work on your reading assignment in your work area.

STUDENT: I don't want to read! It's too hard! (pushes the book away, looking angry)

TUTOR: You need to open the book and start reading the first page.

STUDENT: No! I'm not doing it! (kicks off his shoes)

TUTOR: Please put your shoes back on and look at your book.

STUDENT: (Screams a swear word, pulls off his socks, makes an obscene gesture, and throws the book out of the work area)

options.A: Provide an alternative means for accessing the reading assignment in the work area, such as offering an auditory version of the book or allowing him to use a magnifying device.
options.B: Review the consequence map and give positive verbal praise for appropriate behaviors (e.g., 'Axel, you took off your shoes and used bad words, but then you calmed down'). Then prompt him to return to the reading assignment.
options.C: Allow the use of technology, such as computers or MP-3 players, while he is completing the reading assignment in his individual work area during the academic work session.
options.D: Prompt Axel to use a stress ball if he begins taking off his shoes, swearing, or throwing materials during the reading assignment in his individual work area.
